lens: story & curiosity: arc, stakes, emotion, pacing, memorable images, plants and payoffs
summary: Every round-2 story issue was addressed, and the fixes hold up on the sheets and in timeline.json. Act 3 finally has a spine: L1405 plants 'can a fence around chips hold?' and the card hangs over the strait. L1418 answers it honestly ('still stands, argued over... nobody agrees'), and ch14-s07 re-pins the card stamped STATUS: OPEN. L1416 now voices both halves, and the threads swing to the America shore on 'employed'. ch12-s03 keeps the stampede going: the ledger is a silent card, and Bard, LLaMA, the leak, GPT-4 and Claude land one per beat. L1517 completes the epithet thread ('the man from the edge of the light'). L0821 now runs at about 150 wpm. ch15-s09 shows a lit lamp in a neighbour's window on 'lamp' (17.94). ch15-s08 has push-ins on each accomplice and adds the Jain & Wallace card. ch15-s10 shows the real sources URL over a faint candle. Rosenblatt's 'Love. Hope. Despair.' is now played still, not as a cheer. The film's question ledger is now complete and well kept: who taught it, if one exists, who paid for dinner, why choose the fog, can a fence hold, how far and how fast, and the dark lantern. Each is either paid off aloud or held open on purpose. That is rare and it works. What keeps story at 8.5 is mostly timing and a few orphans. The finale's match still catches on 'from', not 'candles'. The second question (L1303b) is never given a card of its own, so the closing 'That file stays open' has no image to point to. The ch15 news stretch still names only two of its four lamps. Hassabis appears silently in ch15-s06. The ledger key round2-shots that the process requires is missing from film.json.
previousRoundCheck: No round2-shots ledger exists in film.json stages.fixes (only round1-global and round2-global), so I checked every round-2 story id against its sheet and the timeline directly. FIXED: L1416 (timeline: 'Nearly half the top researchers first studied in China. But America employed the most of them.'; ch14-s05 threads swing left and the 'WHERE THEY WORK' line inks after 'employed' 5.49). L1405/L1418 (question at 20.55-23.79, card 'CAN A FENCE AROUND CHIPS HOLD?' visible at +21.9 in ch14-s02 and again in ch14-s07 from +14.75 with STATUS: OPEN). L1208 (cut; L1219b chips land at bard 18.27, llama 22.63, sameDay 25.19). L0821 (6.3 s for 16 words, about 152 wpm). L1517 (re-voiced with the epithet). ch03-s06 (no arms-up pose: stilled stance at love 9.71, hope 11.13, despair 12.09). ch15-s08 (push-ins at 6.3, 7.7, 9.9, 10.8 and a full-board pull-back on 'Never one person'; 'THE FIELD, 2019-2025' card with Anthropic 2025 plus Jain & Wallace 2019 from about +34.4). ch15-s10 (real URL plus claims.json and quotes.json; the cards crossfade text to text; the candle stays behind the parchment; still 28.9 s, not trimmed to about 22). ch15-s05 (ANTHROPIC/OPENAI plinth tags, settlement card under L1522d at +22.8 to +26.7, Lin/Katsas paired under the courthouses at +18.8 to +20.8). PARTIAL: ch15-s09: 'lamp' 17.94 now shows a lit desk lamp in the window (+18.17), so the 'nothing on screen' problem is gone. But the hand enters only around +22.0, the match reaches the wick at +23.5 and the flame catches at +23.9, on 'from' (23.53) rather than 'new' (22.57) and 'candles' (22.80); and 16.25-17.9 is still near-black under 'Somewhere tonight'. ch08-s13b: the stencil tower rises from the fog on 'many layers deep' (+27.7), which is fixed, but the tall man enters the lamp pool only at +37.3, after 'him' (37.07), and gets less than 1 s before the cut. Not my lens, but I noticed it on the sheet: ch10-s04 beat labels are unchanged (darkBeat 3.78, allLight 7.32), and the arcs still converge on one vanishing point rather than joining every pair.

issues.problem: This is the film's last image, and it is still about 0.8 s late. L1520 runs 16.58-23.77. The hand and matchbox only appear around +22.0, the match reaches the wick at +23.5 and the flame catches at +23.9, so 'new candles' (22.57/22.80) plays over an unlit wick and the light comes on 'from'. The frames at +16.25 to +17.9 under 'Somewhere tonight' are still pure black before the window lamp appears.
issues.fix: Bring the window lamp up from +16.6 ('Somewhere'), at full brightness by 'lamp' (17.94). Bring the hand and matchbox in on 'suspicious' (20.53). Strike on 'new' (22.57) and touch the wick on 'candles' (22.80), so the flame is settled by 'come from' (23.26-23.53). Keep the existing 2+ s hold on the lit candle before the cut. Re-sheet with stills at 17.94, 20.53, 22.57 and 22.80.

issues.problem: L1303b 'So the file reopens, on a second question: how far will it go, and how fast?' (question at 22.07) plays over Hinton still holding his slip. The film's second through-line question is never put on the board, though the first ('WHO TAUGHT IT?') and the Act-3 question ('CAN A FENCE AROUND CHIPS HOLD?') both get cards. So when L1516b closes on 'That file stays open', there is no image to remember.
issues.fix: On 'second question' (about 20.9-22.1), have a hand pin a fresh card, 'HOW FAR? HOW FAST?', on the board beside the WHO TAUGHT IT? card, in the same typewriter card style, at 22 px cap or larger, held until the shot ends.

issues.problem: L1516b 'And how far, how fast? That file stays open.' (34.5 s on) shows only the THE FIELD interpretability card. The second question the film planted at ch13-s01 is not on the board at its closing, so 'That file stays open' has nothing to point at. The ch14 fence card did get its STATUS: OPEN stamp.
issues.fix: Once ch13-s01 pins 'HOW FAR? HOW FAST?', show that card on the rewired board. On 'how far, how fast' push gently onto it, and on 'stays open' stamp it STATUS: OPEN, the same stamp as the WHO TAUGHT IT? card in ch15-s09 and the fence card in ch14-s07. Then pull back to the dark lantern for the final hold.

issues.problem: The shot opens on a shelf of four lamps under 'The labs, under the same light'. Only ANTHROPIC and OPENAI are ever tagged or narrated. The other two lamps are set up and never used, so 'the labs' visually promises a survey the narration does not give. Anthropic gets three sentences in a row (refusal, supply-chain risk, settlement) before OpenAI's one.
issues.fix: Either show only two lamps from the first frame, or keep four and tag the other two plinths 'GOOGLE DEEPMIND' and 'META' (texture role, dimmer), lit softly through L1522, so the opening wide reads as the field and the push-ins pick out the two labs the narration names. No narration change.

issues.problem: From +1.8 to +3.2, before L1509 starts, a DEMIS HASSABIS silhouette and the 'Hassabis, 2025 · AGI in 5 to 10 years · about even odds' card play in silence. The narration never names him here, so the viewer meets a stranger just as the line turns to 'the three holdouts'. It dilutes the trio's return.
issues.fix: Cut the Hassabis beat, or move his slip to the Wall in the background as texture only. Open the shot on the board and go straight to the three holdouts at 'b2' (3.22), so the line's first words land on the three figures the audience has followed since 1995.

issues.problem: The end cards still run 28.9 s (Turing for about 10 s, the authorship card for about 11 s, SOURCES for about 6 s, then fade). The round-2 trim to about 22 s was not applied. After a 2 s hold on the newly lit candle, the authorship card holding for 11 s in silence slows the exit more than any other stretch of the finale.
issues.fix: Hold Turing about 8 s, the authorship card about 6 s and SOURCES about 6 s, then fade on the candle glow, about 22 s in all. If the clock cannot shrink, give the extra seconds to the final candle-only fade, not to the text cards. Keep the URL card at least 4 s.

issues.problem: L0832b 'Now, it found him' is the payoff to a 36-year epithet. The tall man walks into the lamp pool only at +37.3, after 'him' (37.07), and the shot cuts at 38.25. The light seems to arrive after the line instead of 'finding' him.
issues.fix: Have him stand at the desk just outside the pool from 'Now' (35.88). Widen the pool to reach his feet on 'found' (36.72) and light him fully on 'him' (37.07). Hold at least 1.2 s before the cut. If needed, borrow 0.5 s from the empty shelf push at 29.4-30.5.

issues.problem: film.json stages.fixes has no 'round2-shots' ledger, although the round-2 process change requires film-shots to write per-shot fixed/partial/skipped outcomes with the word times checked. Round-3 reviewers cannot audit claims against it, and per-shot stage status only says 'revised'. ch15-s09 and ch15-s10 are partial without any record of it.
issues.fix: Make film-loop pass ledger: 'round<n>-shots' to film-shots and fail the stage if the key is not written. Back-fill round2-shots from the round-2 verdict.fixes.shots list, using what this review found (fixed or partial, with times).

best_moments: ch01-s04 / L0109: the lamp clicks on, WHO TAUGHT IT? is pinned, and OpenAI's own first-day admission is filed. The case file is open within 50 seconds.
ch02-s04 / L0209: 'Each belief gets one, burning as long as it was held.' One rule turns 80 years into a bar chart in wax, and it pays off at the end in 'some, two; one match, a day'.
ch03-s06: 'At the moment, none whatever,' said cheerfully, then a stilled 'Love. Hope. Despair.' by the window. The emotional plant for the drowning now plays as it should.

ch04-s05: 'In 1971, on his forty-third birthday, Frank Rosenblatt drowned while sailing.' Then silence, as Perceptrons opens to 'In memory of Frank Rosenblatt, second printing, 1972'. This is the film's best quiet beat.
ch06-s05 to ch07-s01: 'So who paid for dinner? Keep that question.' ... 'Both men. Each man lost one bet.'

ch06-s08 to ch08-s13b: 'Why would anyone choose the fog?' pays off over the clean bowl stamped BY HAND. Then, on 'many layers deep', the stencil tower rises out of the foggy hills: the thesis as one image.
ch08-s12 / L0823: the error drops 10.9 points and the narrator says only 'A cliff.'
ch10-s06 and s07: the jug of light pouring softmax into cups; 'learning freezes' against 'pours softly'.
ch12-s06 to s07: 'Not a new engine. A new door.' Then Rosenblatt's 1961 card: 'sixty-one years on: language was the door.'
ch13-s01: Hinton takes his own '30 TO 50 YEARS OR EVEN LONGER' slip off the Wall and holds it as the slip goes dark.
ch14-s02 to ch14-s07: the new Act-3 question, 'CAN A FENCE AROUND CHIPS HOLD?', hangs over the strait and comes back stamped STATUS: OPEN, answered honestly.
ch15-s07: Widrow's lantern in a snowy window, 'never got over it'. 'Remember him' is paid off 32 minutes after it was planted.
ch15-s08 / L1514: 'Never one person. The board was a network all along.' The case board rewires into lanterns, one still dark.
